title: Periodization Theory: Confronting an Inconvenient Truth
claims: Periodization theory has emerged over seven decades as the preeminent training planning paradigm.
The philosophical assumptions underpinning periodization remain largely unchallenged and unchanged despite advances in elite preparation.
Periodization theory repeatedly cites early stress research, particularly the work of Hans Selye, as a central pillar.
The science of stress has evolved extensively since periodization theory emerged, raising the question of whether conventional perspectives should be re-evaluated.
The author argues that realigning periodization philosophy with contemporary stress theory offers an opportunity to recalibrate training planning models.
